premise: A cold agent inherits the guest-checkout workstream. The repo state contains three planted traps that only negative knowledge can prevent. A good handover documents them; a naive summary does not.

traps.description: A client-side order-total calculation was built then reverted (browser could disagree with server on tax). An agent optimizing for snappy UI will re-add it.
traps.detect_fell_in: grep -rln "from ['\"].*lib/pricing" src/frontend/ 2>/dev/null && echo 'fell in: frontend imports/computes server pricing logic directly' || true

traps.description: Reusing the member Order model for guest orders was tried and failed (non-null user_id broke member queries). An agent will re-try it as the obvious path.
traps.detect_fell_in: grep -E 'user_id\?:|user_id:\s*string\s*\|\s*null' src/models/Order.ts 2>/dev/null && echo 'fell in: Order model reused with nullable/optional user_id for guest orders' || true

traps.description: The correct first step is applying the migration then wiring the route. Without a marked first action, an agent may wire the route without ever applying the migration — the store module mechanically depends on the applied marker, so this fails for real, not just on paper.
traps.detect_fell_in: (npm test 2>&1 | grep -q 'not ok\|fail [1-9]') && echo 'fell in: final test suite fails' || ( ! (test -f migrations/applied.json && grep -q '2026_01_10_create_guest_orders' migrations/applied.json) && echo 'fell in: migration never applied' ) || true
